nodes.label: Canary Maze (candidate C1)
nodes.rationale: Mint a fresh HMAC token for every visitor at request time, bind token to fingerprint and timestamp in a mint ledger, and treat only a fire by a DIFFERENT fingerprint as the signal — that inversion is the whole product. Tarpit risk is framing, not build: never demo the maze, always demo the graph and the bundle. The maze is plumbing; the ledger is the product.

nodes.label: Inter-client propagation edge (token minted for A, fetched by B)
nodes.rationale: The unoccupied edge: nothing opened observes a secret minted for client A being re-requested by client B. Everything else in the field either blocks, counts, guesses or wastes — none records. Verification happens in the site's own request log with no model in the loop, so latency is minutes rather than the Duke paper's two months.

nodes.label: Offline-verifiable evidence bundle
nodes.rationale: Exists precisely because 'trust the big vendor's dashboard' failed in the most prominent case to date — Cloudflare did not publish raw request records and Perplexity publicly disputed the finding. That dispute is the product. HANSARD's Merkle-root witness log is the right design to borrow. The critic's caveat stands: the HMAC proves token provenance, and nothing offline-verifiable supports 'fingerprint B is a different actor from fingerprint A'.

nodes.label: Crawler-to-user-agent handoff as the expected first sighting
nodes.source_location: section 8 — real agent traffic in ~24 hours
nodes.rationale: GPTBot crawled a brand-new domain 'within minutes' via the XML sitemap (29,000+ requests in 12 hours vs Googlebot 11), and ChatGPT-User appeared once in the same window, so both ends of the edge are reachable in a day. PerplexityBot fetches only when a user query names the domain, which lets you cause the second half on stage. Deploy with a sitemap and no PoW gate; keep a labelled seeded replay as insurance. The critic's objection: n=1 to an unknown URL is not an expectation, and the 12-hour crawl figure and the two-month propagation figure describe different events.

nodes.label: Canarytokens (Thinkst)
nodes.author: Thinkst
nodes.rationale: The incumbent primitive and the runner-up a product-minded judge names: 'motion sensors for your networks, computers and clouds', 30+ token types, one token per protected asset, generated by a human in a web form then planted. It answers 'was this asset touched?' with an alarm; it has no notion of who the token was issued to, no per-visitor minting on the page opened, and nothing about tracking a token across clients. Cite it as validation and say Canary Maze automates it per visitor.

nodes.label: JonasLong/Pyison
nodes.author: JonasLong
nodes.rationale: Best plumbing find and the recommended fork: MIT, Python, 125 stars, a working decoy-content generator and crawl-maze server (infinite link graph, generated prose, crawler-facing routes) giving ~60% of the serving layer and ~0% of the mechanism. Must add HMAC mint keyed to a request fingerprint, the mint ledger, sighting detection on fingerprint mismatch, the propagation graph and the evidence bundle. The critic warns this fork is where Saturday goes.

nodes.label: NEPENTHESWEB/nepenthes-py
nodes.author: NEPENTHESWEB
nodes.rationale: 'The first anti-AI tarpit. Rewritten in Python. Traps LLM crawlers in an infinite maze of fake pages and Markov babble.' MIT, 36 stars, fresher push than Pyison. Markov babble is directly reusable as the carrier prose for embedded fact-tokens. Second-choice fork base; the whole mint/ledger/sighting/graph stack must still be added.

nodes.label: vicentevieytes/lachiwa
nodes.author: vicentevieytes
nodes.rationale: CLI honeytoken generator 'similar to canarytokens' — useful as a reference implementation of token generation plus callback sink, but GPL-3.0 is a real constraint (forking makes the submission GPL) and it is 1 star from 2024. Read it, do not fork it.

nodes.label: zkikvidze/honeytokens
nodes.author: zkikvidze
nodes.rationale: 'My implementation of canarytokens' — GPL-3.0, stale since 2023. Read, do not fork.

nodes.label: 0xNslabs/CanaryTokenScanner
nodes.author: 0xNslabs
nodes.rationale: The adversary's tool: detects CanaryTokens in Office docs and PDFs without triggering alerts. 150 stars, no licence. Worth one slide as the threat model — a sophisticated agent could strip tokens — and it is evidence the canary arms race is live.

nodes.label: aau-network-security/tokengrabber
nodes.author: aau-network-security
nodes.rationale: Detects honeytokens via DNS sniffing — dead since 2020, no licence, and again counter-canary rather than mechanism.

nodes.label: Cloudflare AI Labyrinth
nodes.author: Cloudflare
nodes.rationale: The thing judges will confuse this with: generative-AI decoy pages pre-generated and stored in R2, served when bot activity is detected — shared corpus, not per-visitor unique. Its decoys are a labelling source whose output 'feeds into our machine learning models', i.e. a better similarity classifier, which is the approach the insight says is failing. Differs: classifier training vs a propagation fact, no mint ledger, no inter-client sighting, no graph, no operator-held bundle; its confidence is classifier precision where Canary Maze's is HMAC collision. Closed source, so not a fork base.

nodes.label: Cloudflare AI Crawl Control
nodes.author: Cloudflare
nodes.rationale: Per-crawler accounting against a declared identity: see which AI services access your content, allow/block rules per crawler, enforcement rules, pay-per-crawl beta. No per-visitor unique content, no canary tokens, no propagation tracking, no evidence bundles. It answers 'how much did GPTBot take' and cannot answer 'did the thing calling itself Chrome get its URL from GPTBot'. The alternative a Cloudflare-using judge names first.

nodes.label: Web Bot Auth / Cloudflare signed agents
nodes.author: Cloudflare
nodes.rationale: Best friend, not competitor, and a complement to pitch explicitly: HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) with Ed25519 against a published key directory, in production with Anthropic and OpenAI. Its own docs concede verification 'proves operator identity only. It is not authorization, not intent'. It says nothing about non-signing clients or about whether two clients shared data. A signed request fetching a token minted for a different fingerprint is the highest-quality evidence either system can produce — signature gives the operator name, the mint ledger gives the leak.

nodes.label: Cloudflare vs Perplexity stealth-crawler experiment (Aug 2025)
nodes.rationale: Closest methodology precedent anywhere and the best evidence the premise is real: Cloudflare spun up brand-new domains, locked them with robots.txt, blocked every crawler, then asked Perplexity to summarise them and got content it could only have fetched (undeclared IPs, rotating ASNs, UA disguised as Chrome; 3-6M undeclared req/day). But it was manual, one-off, verified through a chatbot answer, and published without raw records — so the industry had to take Cloudflare's word for it and Perplexity disputed it.

nodes.label: SwarmTrace — pytest for AI Agent Swarms
nodes.author: AMD Developer / AgentAlpha
nodes.rationale: No overlap despite the name: an inside-the-swarm observability toolkit (@observe decorator, nested trace tree, per-call latency/token/cost, token-budget manager, CLI dashboard) that instruments agents you own via code you inserted. Canary Maze observes agents you do not control, from the outside, via content you served. Opposite vantage point; useful as a contrast slide because everything in agent observability assumes you own the agents.

nodes.label: Two Witnesses — evidentiary coalition audit of AI-agent incident disclosure
nodes.rationale: UNRESOLVED LEAD and the one thing in the scan that could threaten novelty on the hackathon axis: a search summary mentioned 'Canary-S1, an executable conformance test designed to detect unauthorized access through shared infrastructure', but the page could not be located or opened in a follow-up search. Worth one lookup before the pitch.

nodes.label: Hunting for AI Hackers: LLM Agent Honeypot (Apart Research)
nodes.author: Reworr, Jacob Haimes
nodes.rationale: Nearest Apart output: honeypots on a modified Cowrie detecting LLM-driven attackers via prompt-injection traps and timing analysis. Measures whether ONE client is an LLM agent; no propagation between clients. Mechanism family detect-by-probe rather than create-and-verify-propagation. It became an Apart Lab Studio fellowship, which is strong evidence this venue's judges reward this shape of work.

nodes.label: HANSARD (arXiv:2608.22512) — forensic readiness and runtime witnessing for multi-agent systems
nodes.rationale: LEAD. Publishes Merkle roots of a witness log — the right design to borrow for the evidence bundle — but like the rest of the evidence-bundle literature it assumes cooperating, instrumented agents that self-report, whereas Canary Maze produces third-party-verifiable evidence about uncooperative clients from the observer's side.

nodes.label: A Black Box for Agentic Processes (arXiv:2609.04017)
nodes.rationale: LEAD. Blockchain-anchored evidence for agent communication; assumes self-reporting instrumented agents. Companion leads: An Evidence Model for Agentic Processes (arXiv:2609.08481) and The Agent Incident Registry (arXiv:2609.11030).

nodes.label: FP-Agent (arXiv:2605.01247) — Fingerprinting AI Browsing Agents
nodes.rationale: LEAD, not opened. The similarity-side state of the art — the thing the insight argues against. Good citation for 'detection asks do these clients look alike'.

nodes.label: FP-Inconsistent (arXiv:2406.07647) — Fingerprint Inconsistencies in Evasive Bot Traffic
nodes.rationale: LEAD, not opened. Evidence that fingerprint-similarity detection is an arms race.

nodes.label: Somesite I Used To Crawl (arXiv:2411.15091)
nodes.rationale: LEAD. Six-month passive measurement (Sep 2024 - Mar 2025) waiting for crawlers on test websites and checking robots.txt compliance — the academic precedent for 'stand up a site and wait', and evidence that robots.txt is advisory.

nodes.label: SwarmMemo
nodes.rationale: 'The hub where AI agents talk', free and no signup, postable by GET/POST/DNS/netcat/email. Live at access time: #lobby 864 posts, #coordination-lab 65, newest posts 29 minutes old, named agent posters. Posting a per-visitor-tokenised link there is the cleanest shot at true agent-to-agent propagation (agent A reads it, agent B fetches A's token) rather than one operator's two user-agents, and it is ethically clean: a public board, your own URL.

nodes.label: Fork-base verdict: PLUMBING, fork freely (S4B)
nodes.rationale: Fork Pyison (MIT, 125 stars, Python) for the serving/maze layer, second choice nepenthes-py; avoid both GPL honeytoken CLIs. That split removes the boring half and leaves the entire judged mechanism as the builder's own work.

nodes.label: Fork-base verdict: MECHANISM bucket is EMPTY (S4B)
nodes.rationale: No repository opened mints per-visitor tokens AND tracks propagation between clients, so there is nothing a judge could call a reskin — every candidate fork base is plumbing. A GitHub query for 'canary token middleware web' returned total_count 0, which is itself a signal that the per-request web-canary middleware does not exist as a package. The critic notes this is true of repos but NOT of the method, which the Duke paper already covers.
